sections.h2: Where Winston-Salem owners take tax questions
sections.html:
A Winston-Salem home is taxed through Forsyth County Tax Administration, which handles appeals, relief applications and ownership questions. The office is at 201 N. Chestnut Street in the Forsyth County Government Center, and the phone is 336-703-2300. The same counter hands out appeal and relief forms.

Before you call, write down the parcel number so the clerk can pull your file in one step. The county's real estate page suggests having the parcel number, the owner's full name and the street address ready before you call the appraisal section. Appraisal records can be bought for 50 cents a page. If you want to know how a city levy shows up on your bill, ask the tax office.

The city has an estimated 257,271 residents for 2025, up 3.1% from the 249,549 counted in April 2020, spread across roughly 133 square miles.

  • Owners occupy 55.6% of homes, which leaves nearly half in rental use.
  • The typical owned home is valued at $233,800, and typical gross rent is $1,087.
  • Monthly owner costs run a median $1,459 with a mortgage and $486 without.

The 2020 count works out to about 1,880 residents on each of the city's 132.7 square miles of land, so values vary a lot from block to block. These are city-wide averages. A house on one street can sit far from them, and a house needing repairs may carry an assessed value higher than its likely sale price. That gap is a reason to review the assessment before you list. Anyone weighing the cost of holding a vacant house should add the tax bill, insurance and upkeep to the averages above.

The September 1 due date is followed by a grace period, and face value payments are accepted through the day before January 6. From January 6 interest is 2% until February begins, then three-fourths of a percent every month. A mailed check is judged by its USPS postmark date.

Sellers should know who gets the bill: the January 1 titleholder. If you close later in the year, you are still the liable party on paper. The closing usually prorates the tax, and the county advises confirming with your realtor or attorney that it was done.

Put your appeal to the Forsyth County review board in writing. It must arrive or be postmarked after January 1 and no later than the last business day in June. The form is online and at the Tax Office.

The board follows state hearing rules. A reappraisal year can shift the calendar, so confirm the date with the office before you file. If you want to challenge the value, decide before you list, because the window closes in the middle of the selling season. Gather recent nearby sales, repair estimates and photos, and attach them to the written appeal so the board has something concrete to weigh.

Forsyth County administers three relief programs, and an owner may use just one of them. The cutoff for applications is June 1 every year.

North Carolina relief programs available to Winston-Salem owners
ProgramWho qualifiesWhat it does
Elderly or disabled exclusionAt least 65, or fully and permanently disabled, with income up to $38,800Shelters half the value or $25,000, whichever is larger
Disabled veteran exclusionA disabled veteran or an unmarried surviving spouseExcludes $45,000 of value
Circuit breaker defermentMeets the same age or disability test, has owned and lived there five years, income under $58,200Tax limited to 4% or 5% of income, rest deferred as a lien

You can get an application from the Tax Office or online. For a home with several non-spouse owners, all of them must meet the standards for the circuit breaker.

sections.h2: Back tax on a Winston-Salem house
sections.html:
Unpaid tax stays with the property. The lien takes hold on the January 1 listing date, and penalties, interest and costs pile on beside it. If it goes unpaid long enough the county can seek a court-ordered sale, and selling first avoids that. Owners who inherit a house should look for back years too, since each year adds its own lien and interest. Ask the Tax Office to list every open year for the parcel, not only the current one, so the payoff is complete. The closing agent pays it out of your proceeds.

  • Ask the county for the exact balance on your parcel.
  • Make sure the attorney lists it on the settlement sheet.
  • File proof of payment with your closing papers.

Forsyth County also covers owners outside the city limits, so make sure the bill and records you pull are for your own parcel. The city grew from 229,617 residents in the 2010 census to 249,545 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 257,271. About 85.3% of residents kept the same address over the prior year, so the population is fairly settled and many owners have held their homes for years. Such owners may not have seen a market price in a long time, which makes recent nearby sales worth checking against your assessment.

A disabled owner who meets the state test may qualify for the $45,000 exclusion, and the Tax Office can explain the steps.

sections.h2: Circuit breaker deferrals and a sale
sections.html:
A deferral becomes a lien, so it has to be cleared when the house sells. Under the circuit breaker program, the part of the tax above the income cap is deferred. That amount accrues interest and is added to the property as a lien.

If you qualify, ask the Tax Office for the full deferred balance before listing. It shows up in the title search, and the closing agent pays it from your proceeds. The program also requires five years of owning and occupying the home, and a new application each year.

  • Income of $38,800 or less pays 4% of income.
  • Income above that, up to $58,200, pays 5% of income.
  • Any tax above those amounts is deferred and carries interest.

sections.h2: Planning a sale around tax dates
sections.html:
Line up your closing with the tax year. A spring closing happens after the date that fixed the owner, so the seller's name sits on that year's bill even when the buyer moves in during March.

An inherited or empty house follows the same rule, and unpaid amounts keep growing through interest. Before you list, call the Tax Office at 336-703-2300, get the balance, and settle with the buyer on who pays what. If the closing lands in the weeks after the bill goes out, the buyer will likely want a copy of it for their own records.

1. Get the parcel number and the current balance from Forsyth County.
  2. Ask whether any relief deferral is on the account.
  3. Check that your attorney's settlement sheet prorates the bill.
  4. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

A cash buyer still expects the tax to be handled at closing, so these steps apply however the sale is financed, though a cash deal skips the lender's appraisal and can close sooner.

faqs.q: Which number reaches Winston-Salem's tax office?
faqs.a: Call Forsyth County Tax Administration at 336-703-2300. The office is in the Forsyth County Government Center at 201 N. Chestnut Street.

faqs.q: When does a Winston-Salem appeal window end?
faqs.a: The last business day in June. Check with the office about the year you are filing, since a reappraisal year can shift the calendar.

faqs.q: Will I owe tax after a spring sale?
faqs.a: Possibly. The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, and the closing normally splits the cost between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: When does interest start on unpaid Winston-Salem tax?
faqs.a: Interest starts on January 6, at 2% until February 1 and three-fourths of a percent per month after that.

faqs.q: Can I get a lower tax bill as a senior or a disabled veteran?
faqs.a: Maybe. All three state programs need an application and cannot be stacked. Ask whether you meet the age, disability or veteran tests, since the answer changes which one fits.
